findings.assertion: On 9 February 1913, forces loyal to Madero under Lauro Villar recaptured the National Palace from the rebel Aspirants; INEHRM records the 20th and 24th infantry battalions defending the site and troops, machine guns and mortars positioned to protect palace entrances and roof.
findings.source_locator: INEHRM exhibition 'La recuperación de Palacio Nacional', text by photograph of palace defenders and SINAFO no.287566
findings.limitations: Photo of palace defense is a curated reproduction, not proof of surviving physical firing positions.

findings.assertion: The Ciudadela served as the rebels' fortified military depot after the failed 9 February palace assault; INEHRM describes a frontal attack on 11 February, with fire from emplacements in the depot and nearby street mouths.
findings.source_locator: INEHRM exhibition 'Escenarios de guerra. La Ciudadela', artillery photograph Sabino Osuna SINAFO no.451537 and 11 Feb paragraph
findings.limitations: The exhibition's battlefield reconstruction should be checked against military dispatches; present-day building layout must not be equated with 1913 configuration.

findings.assertion: The INEHRM exhibition includes a photograph catalogued by SINAFO as no.37342 depicting war-damaged buildings on Avenida Juárez in February 1913, documenting material damage beyond the Ciudadela itself.
findings.source_locator: INEHRM exhibition 'Huellas de la guerra. La ciudad de México', Avenida Juárez photo caption, SINAFO 37342
findings.limitations: Exact buildings in photograph not independently geolocated; absence of confirmed modern survivors.

findings.assertion: INEHRM identifies the Madero family house on Avenida Berlín in Colonia Juárez as burned on 14 February 1913 and reproduces Miret photographs of the property after the fire.
findings.source_locator: INEHRM exhibition 'Huellas de la guerra. La casa de Francisco I. Madero'; photograph by Félix Miret, credited to AGN
findings.limitations: Exact historic house number and any present-day remnant not verified; cannot use as a live location pin without address research.

findings.assertion: A photograph credited to Manuel Ramos and the Elmer and Diane Powell collection at Southern Methodist University shows civilians leaving a conflict zone with a white flag during February 1913.
geographies: Central Mexico City; precise intersection unknown
findings.source_locator: INEHRM exhibition PDF indexed p.12 'La población civil', upper photograph and credit line
findings.limitations: Image attribution and caption from curator; precise locality and identities of persons undetermined; photo rights not cleared.

findings.assertion: INEHRM reproduces a SINAFO photograph catalogued no.37465 with the caption 'Incineración de cadáveres en Balbuena, febrero de 1913', evidence for a documented emergency response to deaths in the capital during fighting.
findings.source_locator: INEHRM exhibition PDF indexed p.13 (caption adjacent to civilian casualties), SINAFO no.37465
findings.limitations: No verified death count or exact location; caption is evidence for image attribution, not independent confirmation of all circumstances.

findings.assertion: The INEHRM exhibition identifies a photographed fire and looting episode at the newspaper Nueva Era during February 1913 (SINAFO image no.451515), illustrating direct disruption of the capital's press during the coup.
findings.source_locator: INEHRM exhibition PDF indexed p.14 'La prensa y la noticia nacional', photographic caption, SINAFO no.451515
findings.limitations: Photograph and institutional description verified; precise building location, attack responsibility and image reuse rights require research.

findings.assertion: An INEHRM exhibition reproduction shows the Diario Oficial issue of 20 February 1913, documenting formal publication of the transfer of executive authority after the coerced resignations on 19 February.
findings.source_locator: INEHRM exhibition PDF indexed p.20 showing Diario Oficial front page, adjacent institutional narrative
findings.limitations: Facsimile in a modern exhibit, not a direct inspection of the original complete issue; legal mechanism needs textual analysis of original parliamentary records.

findings.assertion: INEHRM's exhibition describes the 16 February 1913 temporary armistice as permitting civilians to leave the fighting area and records that hostilities resumed around 2 p.m., earlier than planned.
findings.source_locator: INEHRM exhibition 'El armisticio', Casasola SINAFO no.5664 and adjacent explanation
findings.limitations: Exact operational timing based on exhibition; seek original military communiqué and contemporary press accounts before presenting minute-specific reconstruction.
